problems: The Nile ribbon and its reflections touch the bottom edge, so the subject is not entirely within the middle 60% of the image height.
Plum (#B07D9C) is not the dominant colour; teal and ochre occupy most of the area.
fix: Keep the 3:2 canvas and cream paper (#F3EBDB). 1) Select all subject layers (river, boat, pyramids, sun, palms, buildings, hills, reflections) and group them. Uniformly scale the group down by ~10–15% and reposition it so the lowest element sits above the 20% bottom margin and the highest below the 80% top margin, maintaining the current asymmetric layout. 2) To make plum dominant without violating the ochre-desert requirement or the four-ink limit, add a 20–30% plum (#B07D9C) halftone overprint across the broad desert planes and riverbanks and strengthen the plum fill on the pyramids and distant mesas; leave the river teal, palms/lines charcoal, and the sun ochre. Change nothing else.

problems: Letter-like emblem (resembles an 'H') on the ship’s stern violates the no text/letters rule
fix: Remove the letter-like emblem on the ship’s stern. Replace it with a simple non-letter geometric motif (e.g., a small plum #B07D9C triangle or chevron) or leave the stern plain. Use only the existing inks and do not alter any other elements.

problems: Modern triangular‑sailed yacht in the bay is anachronistic for 480–323 BCE
fix: Replace the current white triangular‑sailed yacht with an ancient Aegean craft: a small hull with a single mast and a square sail (and optional oars), drawn in the same flat cut‑paper style using only the specified inks (charcoal #22211F, plum #B07D9C, blue #8AA7C4, olive #A3AA6A) and the cream paper for negative space. Keep the boat’s scale and position in the bay, and change nothing else.

problems: The two central flights run down towards each other into a V-shaped valley with no landing, which is an impossible stair; Persepolis double stairs rise towards each other to a shared landing at the top.
fix: Redraw the central double stair so its two flights rise from the ground towards each other and meet at a shared landing at terrace level (an inverted V), each flight starting at ground level on the outside. Keep the relief panels, terrace, columns and figures. Change nothing else.

problems: The main subject (staff and ring of elders) extends into the bottom 20% of the canvas, so it is not entirely within the middle 60% of the height
fix: Select the entire subject group—the central staff with cord, tassels and horn, plus all six seated elders and their immediate ground patches/tufts—and move it upward so that the lowest element sits above the bottom 20% of the canvas. Ensure the highest element also remains below the top 20%, keeping all colors, textures, background landscape, and composition otherwise unchanged.

problems: Text-like glyphs inside the jar’s circular seal violate the no-text rule
Seal appears as a medallion on the jar’s body instead of a clay sealing on the stopper/neck, which is historically inaccurate for Uruk-period jars
fix: On the jar at the foot of the stairs, delete the glyphs inside the circular mark so no letters or numerals remain. Move this circular mark from the body to the jar’s mouth/neck and render it as a simple clay plug or lump over the opening with a plain ring-shaped impression (no characters). Optionally indicate a short sealing cord under the rim using existing inks. Keep colors to charcoal #22211F, indigo #8F88B8, ochre #D9A441 and teal #5E9C97 on the warm cream paper, maintain the current composition and all other elements unchanged.

problems: Ishtar Gate–like blue-glazed animal panels on the city gate are anachronistic for a Sumerian Ur III city
fix: Remove the Neo-Babylonian-style decoration on the main gate: paint over the blue rectangular panels and the two animal relief silhouettes with ochre #D9A441, matching the surrounding mudbrick walls; keep the gate’s shape and shadows by using charcoal #22211F for edges and recesses. Do not add any new motifs—leave the gate plain buttressed mudbrick. Change nothing else in the image, palette, composition, or textures.

problems: Barley fields and irrigation channels extend into the bottom 20% of the canvas, outside the required middle 60% height.
Smoke plume rises into the top 20% of the canvas, breaching the subject-inside-middle-60% rule.
fix: Mask or crop the lowest rows of barley and the foreground irrigation channels so no subject elements fall below the bottom 20% of the canvas; keep field edges and spacing consistent. Shorten or bend the smoke plume so its top terminates below the top 20% margin while preserving its wispy shape and sage/charcoal halftone texture. Do not move or resize other elements; keep the 3:2 layout, palette (#22211F, #D9A441, #9DB592, #C9705C) and style unchanged.

problems: Shields read as separate objects behind the warriors rather than being carried; no visible hands/straps connect them to the figures
Depth inconsistency where some shield edges overlap legs while the torsos appear in front, creating an impossible layering
fix: For each warrior, move the tall rectangular shield forward so it is clearly being carried. Add a simple charcoal (#22211F) hand or vertical strap/grip at the shield’s inside edge, and have the shield overlap the warrior’s forearm/torso and partially occlude the near leg to make the carry unambiguous. Ensure all shields align consistently behind the spear shafts (no shield edges crossing in front of legs while torsos remain in front). Keep the four-ink palette, flat mid-century style, composition, and all other elements unchanged.

problems: Seven men but only six shields; the rearmost man has none.
The men shrink from back to front of the file while their feet stay on one baseline and the shields stay the same size.
Stray orange legs show among the black ones.
fix: Make every man the same height, his helmet the same size, with all feet on one baseline. Give each man one shield, seven in all. Make every leg the same black. Change nothing else.

problems: Arrow trajectories extend into the top 20% of the canvas, placing part of the subject outside the required middle 60% height band.
fix: Select the three dotted arrow arcs and their arrowheads. Nudge each arc downward so that every dot and arrowhead sits between 20% and 80% of the canvas height, maintaining their relative spacing and curvature. Do not alter the archers, bows, landscape, colours, textures, or any other elements.

problems: Visible wheel has five spokes instead of the required six
Harness lacks a visible yoke saddle across the horses’ withers; hitching resembles a breastcollar rather than a New Kingdom yoke
fix: Redraw the chariot’s visible wheel to have six evenly spaced spokes, keeping its size, position, and color unchanged. Add a proper New Kingdom yoke: a straight wooden yoke mounted on two saddle pads resting across both horses’ withers, joined to a central pole from the chariot axle between the horses. Adjust or remove the breastcollar-like chest straps so the traces correctly attach to the yoke/pole. Preserve all other elements, composition, and the four-ink color palette.

problems: Subject extends outside the middle 60% of the height; the feet are too close to the bottom edge.
fix: On the existing 3:2 cream (#F3EBDB) canvas, uniformly scale down the entire group of swordsmen and shields or nudge it upward so that the highest helmets and lowest feet both lie fully within the central 60% of the canvas height (leave at least a 20% margin at top and bottom). Change nothing else: keep the flattened style, composition, and the four inks (charcoal #22211F, dominant bronze #A97F63, indigo #8F88B8, brick #C9705C), with no added text, borders, gradients, or effects.

problems: Subject not entirely within the middle 60% of the height (sun/clouds reach into the top band; foreground grass approaches the bottom band).
fix: Group all illustrated elements (tree, grass, rocks, horizon, sun, clouds). Uniformly scale the group down and reposition it so every element sits between 20% and 80% of the canvas height, leaving clear cream-paper margins above and below. Do not change colors, inks, style, or aspect ratio.

problems: Boat shows a triangular (lateen) sail, anachronistic for Sumer–Babylonia where square sails were used
fix: Replace the triangular sail with a square sail hung from a horizontal yard across the mast, appropriate to Mesopotamian boats. Redraw the simple rigging and the sail’s reflection on the water to match the new square sail. Keep the cut-paper style, composition, and the four-ink palette unchanged.

problems: Foreground scrub and dunes touch the bottom edge, so the subject is not entirely within the middle 60% of the image height
fix: Translate the entire illustrated subject band (dunes, scrub, figures, goats, shoreline, and distant village) upward just enough that the lowest vegetation sits above the bottom 20% margin, keeping all subject matter entirely within the central 60% of the canvas height. Maintain the 3:2 canvas, colors, textures, and all other elements unchanged.

problems: Triangular lateen sails on the Nile boats are anachronistic for Ancient Egypt (3000–300 BCE); they should use square sails.
fix: On all sailboats, replace the triangular lateen rigs with ancient Egyptian square sails: add a single horizontal yard on a central mast and hang a rectangular sail (use the paper colour with charcoal outlines). Adjust each boat’s water reflection to match the new square-sail silhouette. Keep positions, sizes, colours, textures, and all other elements unchanged.

problems: Water lily pads are ellipses/ovals rather than circles as specified.
fix: Redraw the water lily pads as perfect circles (no perspective foreshortening). Keep each pad’s center position and approximate diameter the same, use olive #A3AA6A (with allowed overprint/texture) and only the specified inks. Do not change any other elements.

problems: Foreground and distant boats use triangular lateen sails, anachronistic for Ancient Egypt (should be square sails).
fix: Replace all triangular sails with square Egyptian river sails appropriate to 3000–300 BCE: add a horizontal yard across the top of each sail on the existing mast, with a rectangular sail panel hanging below. Keep hulls, positions, proportions, and all inks (#22211F, #9DB592, #8AA7C4, #D9A441) and textures unchanged; do not move any other elements.

problems: Distant hills and water shapes use a bluish teal tone outside the specified four-ink palette
fix: Recolor the distant hills, water/terrace shapes, and any similarly bluish elements to use only the approved inks: sage #9DB592 and olive #A3AA6A (with permissible halftone for lighter values), bronze #A97F63 where appropriate, and charcoal #22211F for lines/shadows. Remove the bluish-teal hue so every shape matches one of these inks or their halftone tints, changing nothing else.

problems: Oriental plane tree is missing; only a willow (and cypress-like trees) is shown.
The subject extends outside the middle 60% of the height—the mirrored tree silhouettes reach close to the bottom edge.
fix: Add a stylised Oriental plane tree at the lakeshore beside the willow, with a broad, spreading crown and palmate leaves; render it in the same flat mid-century cut-paper style using only the specified inks (#22211F, #9DB592 dominant, #8AA7C4, #A3AA6A). Add its mirrored silhouette directly below in the water. Then slightly reduce the vertical scale of the trees and their reflections by about 10–15% and nudge the group upward so that the highest canopies sit below the upper 20% of the canvas and the lowest points of the reflections sit above the lower 20%, keeping the entire subject within the central 60% band. Do not alter the palette, composition balance, or any other elements (hills, temple, negative space).

problems: Subject extends into the bottom 20% of the canvas; not entirely within the middle 60% of the height
fix: On the existing 3:2 cream (#F3EBDB) canvas, select the entire illustrated valley/terraces artwork as one layer. Uniformly scale it down slightly (about 10–15%) and move it upward just enough so that all painted elements fall between 20% and 80% of the canvas height, leaving clear empty margins at top and bottom. Do not change colors, textures, composition, or add any new elements.

problems: Parts of the subject (lake edge and foreground rocks/flowers) extend into the lower 20% of the image height, violating the “subject entirely inside the middle 60%” requirement
fix: Uniformly scale the entire illustrated scene (mountains, lake, reflections, foreground rocks and flowers) down by about 10–15% and reposition it so all subject elements fall between 20% and 80% of the canvas height. Keep the 3:2 canvas, fill any newly revealed areas with the same warm cream #F3EBDB, and change nothing else (palette, textures, composition otherwise).

problems: The subject (ziggurat, temple, rings) is not entirely within the middle 60% of the image height; the outer rings reach into the top 20% and the base sits near the bottom 20%
fix: Select the entire subject group (ziggurat, all three stairs, summit temple, concentric rings, and their shadows). Uniformly scale it down by about 10–15% and reposition it so the highest point (top of the outer ring) is below the top 20% line and the lowest point (base of the ziggurat) is above the bottom 20% line, keeping the current horizontal placement. Do not alter the palette, background, palms, water, textures, or any other elements.

problems: Bright yellow accents on vines/foliage introduce a fifth ink outside the specified palette
Parts of the subject (shaduf water pool) touch the bottom edge, so the subject is not entirely within the middle 60% of the height
fix:
1) Recolor: Select all bright yellow fills used in vine berries/flower tips and any similar accents. Replace them with approved inks—preferably olive #A3AA6A (use solid or a light halftone) or sage #9DB592. Do not introduce any hue outside charcoal #22211F, olive #A3AA6A, sage #9DB592, and blue #8AA7C4; achieve variation only by overprint/halftone of these inks.
2) Vertical placement: Group the entire subject (terraced gardens, foliage, shaduf and its water flow/pool, distant blue palace). Move the group upward so that the lowest edge of the blue water sits above the lower 20% of the canvas height while keeping the highest point of the terraces below the upper 20%. If this crowds the top, uniformly scale the grouped subject down by ~5–10% to fit entirely within the middle 60% band. Change nothing else.

problems: Anachronistic Greek-style peristyle temple with a pediment atop the island; inappropriate for Phoenician Tyre (1000–600 BCE).
fix: Replace the hilltop Greek temple with a Phoenician sanctuary appropriate to 1000–600 BCE: a rectangular cella set within a small walled court, flat or slightly pitched roof, no classical pediment or peristyle; a short porch with two free‑standing columns or obelisk-like pylons is fine. Keep the same scale, placement, and the four-ink palette (charcoal, olive dominant, blue, plum) and mid-century flat style. Do not alter any other elements.

problems: Lighthouse middle tier is not clearly octagonal; the tower reads as a continuous square shaft rather than three distinct tiers
fix: Redraw the lighthouse so it has three distinct tiers: keep the lower tier clearly square, then introduce a separate, shorter octagonal middle tier with eight visible facets indicated by facet edges and alternating olive/charcoal overprint shadows, and retain the cylindrical lantern and statue above. Preserve the existing palette (#22211F, #A3AA6A, #8AA7C4, #D9A441) and all other elements, composition, proportions, and textures unchanged.

problems: The horse’s saddle has a modern shaped seat with pommel/cantle, anachronistic for Achaemenid Persia; it should be a simple pad/blanket.
The bridle/headstall looks complex (browband/noseband); the prompt calls for a simple headstall.
The distant ruins read as a Greco‑Roman colonnade/temple rather than Achaemenid Persian architecture.
fix: Redraw the tack: replace the modern saddle with a thick rectangular pad/blanket secured by a plain girth (optional simple breast strap), with no rigid tree, pommel, cantle or knee rolls; keep colours within charcoal, olive, ochre and brick. Simplify the headstall to a single-strap bridle (cheekpieces to a simple bit and a throatlatch only), or show a plain rope halter; remove the noseband and other modern hardware, and tie the lead to the halter/headstall rather than the bit. Modify the far-right architecture by removing the Greco-Roman pediment/temple look and substituting Achaemenid features: a low terrace with stair, and tall slender columns topped with animal capitals (bull/griffin), keeping scale, placement, and the flat mid-century style and colour palette unchanged.

problems: Background shows a multi-tier ziggurat, which is anachronistic for Ubaid–early Uruk (5000–3500 BCE)
fix: Replace the stepped, multi-tier ziggurat in the distant background with architecture appropriate to Ubaid–early Uruk: a low, single raised mudbrick platform or a modest tripartite temple on a single terrace with simple buttresses, or a cluster of low reed/mudbrick houses. Keep the same placement and scale, the 4-ink palette (charcoal #22211F, olive #A3AA6A, sage #9DB592, ochre #D9A441) and the mid-century flat style. Change nothing else in the image.

problems: Subject elements (foreground figures and wall) drop into the lower margin, not entirely within the middle 60% of the height
Riverboat uses a triangular/lateen-style sail, anachronistic for Early Dynastic Sumer (should be a square sail)
fix: Uniformly scale the entire precinct and figures down by about 10–12% and nudge upward so the lowest figures’ feet sit above the 20% height line and the highest parapet remains below the 80% line, preserving the 3:2 canvas and the existing four-ink palette on the warm cream ground. Replace the riverboat’s triangular sail with a square sail set on a horizontal yard across a short mast (appropriate to Sumer), keeping the same size, position and inks (teal/cream with charcoal accents) and the flat cut-paper style.

problems: Three reed-bundle boats shown; prompt calls for exactly two
Parts of the subject extend into the bottom 20% of the canvas; the subject must sit entirely within the middle 60% of the height
fix: Remove the small reed-bundle boat at the far right background so only two boats remain (the foreground right boat and the mid-distance right boat). Then select the foreground boat together with its full reflection and the immediately adjacent water ripples, group them, and move this group upward by about 8–10% of the canvas height so that no boat, reflection, reeds, or ripples falls below the lower 20% margin. Do not alter colors, textures, or any other elements.

problems: The subject is not entirely within the middle 60% of the height; the quay and outer waves extend into the bottom margin.
fix: On the existing 3:2 canvas, uniformly scale the entire illustrated scene (quay, ships, breakwater, waves, buildings) down by about 10–15% and move it slightly upward so all elements fall between 20% and 80% of the canvas height. Keep the four-ink palette, style, and all details unchanged; add nothing else.

problems: Axes look like later eye/socket axes rather than Bronze-Age tanged bronze axes
Parts of the subject (tall left tree, foreground shoreline/logs) extend outside the middle 60% of the image height
fix:
- Redraw all axe heads as tanged bronze: a flat bronze (#A97F63) blade with a short tang inserted into a split wooden haft, secured with a simple dark charcoal (#22211F) lashing. Keep silhouettes simple and flat; remove any eye/socket depiction.
- Reposition/scale the composition vertically so the entire subject sits within the middle 60% of the canvas height (between the 20% and 80% height lines). Either slightly reduce the subject’s vertical scale or nudge elements: lower the top of the leftmost tree and raise the lowest shoreline/logs so no figures, trees, logs, or camp structures touch the top or bottom bands. Preserve the 3:2 layout, palette (charcoal, olive #A3AA6A dominant, bronze #A97F63, blue #8AA7C4), and all other details.

problems: The hill between the surface and the tunnel is drawn as one huge black void, with the access shafts standing in it like pillars; a qanat is a narrow tunnel through solid ground.
fix: Fill the black cavity with the hill's solid green ground so the hill is solid. Keep the blue water channel as a narrow tunnel line along the bottom, and draw each vertical shaft as a narrow dark slot cut down through solid ground from its spoil mound to the tunnel. Change nothing else.

problems: Parts of the main subject (worker’s feet and the rake head) fall into the bottom 20% of the frame, violating the “subject entirely inside the middle 60% of the height” rule
The added basket and foreground salt pile also sit in the bottom 20% band
fix: On a separate layer, select the entire foreground subject group (worker, rake and its shadow, the salt patch he’s raking, the basket and foreground salt pile). Uniformly scale this group down by about 5–8% and move it upward by roughly 10–12% of the canvas height so that all of these elements sit entirely within the middle 60% of the image height. Ensure the worker’s head stays below the top 80% line. Do not alter colors, textures, background pans, coastline, boat or buildings, and keep the 3:2 canvas unchanged.

problems: Parts of the subject (cave mouth, miner, and the fire) extend below the middle 60% of the image height; the fire and foreground rocks sit too close to the bottom edge
fix: Group the entire subject (sandstone outcrop with cave opening, miner, wicker basket, fire and adjacent foreground rocks) into one layer. Move this group upward by ~6–8% of the canvas height and, if needed, uniformly scale it down by ~5% so that every element of the subject sits entirely within the central 60% vertical band (between 20% and 80% of the image height). Do not alter colors, textures, or any other elements.

problems: A strip of empty paper runs just under the surface, so the top crust with the windlass and building floats free of the hill.
The left gallery opens straight out of the hill's side into the air.
fix: Fill the pale strip under the surface with the hill's green ground so the surface crust joins the hill. Close the left gallery's outer end with rock so it ends inside the hill. Change nothing else.

problems: Smooth gradient on the heated blade; gradients are not allowed.
Gradient-like shading on the amphora and bowl instead of flat inks/halftone.
Bellows lacks a visible nozzle/tuyère connecting to the coals, making the forge setup unrealistic.
Bellows design appears accordion/box-style, anachronistic for Bronze Age Anatolia; should be simple bag or pot bellows.
fix: Remove all smooth gradients. Repaint the heated blade as flat shapes using only brick and ochre inks with crisp edges (allow a small paper-colour highlight if needed). Repaint the amphora and bowl with flat ochre/brick areas or halftone texture only, no soft blends. Replace the current bellows with a Bronze Age-appropriate leather bag (or pot) bellows placed behind the smith; add a short clay/metal tuyère nozzle that clearly connects from the bellows to the charcoal hearth. Preserve the existing composition, palette (four inks plus paper), style, and keep the subject within the middle 60% of the height; change nothing else.

problems: Banner above the gate contains cuneiform-like text, violating the no-text rule
fix: Remove all text-like glyphs from the banner above the gate. Keep the lamassu emblem, but replace the inscription area with a flat brick-ink (#C9705C) field or a simple non-text decorative stripe using the existing inks. Do not add any other elements or colors; leave all other parts of the image unchanged.

problems: Worker appears to be standing inside a shallow mixing bowl on the ground while sealing the silo top, which is physically implausible
fix: Move the plaster mixing bowl to the ground slightly forward-left of the worker so it does not overlap his legs; keep its size, texture, and shadow consistent. Repose the worker so both feet stand on the curved top of the rightmost silo (ankles making believable contact with the dome). Remove any bowl overlap from his legs and adjust his lower-leg lengths and cast shadows accordingly. Do not change the palette, textures, composition, or any other elements.

problems: Cuneiform-like text marks on the clay tablets violate the 'no text, letters, numbers' rule.
fix: Remove all inscription-like marks from every clay tablet (in the scribe’s hands, on the table, and on the shelves). Repaint the tablet faces as plain ochre shapes using the existing ochre ink with a subtle non-directional texture (stipple or light halftone) so they don’t read as writing. Keep all colors, shapes, composition, and overprint effects unchanged; alter nothing else.

problems: The sun sits on the horizon directly behind the stones, yet the shadows fall sideways to the right and the stones are lit from the left.
fix: With the sun low behind the stones, make every stone's front face (towards the viewer) the dark shadowed face, and make each shadow fall straight towards the viewer from the stone's base. Change nothing else.

problems: Rotary quern shown instead of the specified saddle quern; anachronistic for Old Babylonian Ur.
The subject extends beyond the middle 60% of the image height (top roof figure and bottom wall approach the edges).
fix: Replace the rotary quern with a saddle quern: depict a low rectangular grinding slab with a curved surface and a separate handstone held with both hands, placed on the courtyard floor near the pottery jars. Remove any circular base or vertical handle. Then uniformly scale the entire house-and-figures group down by about 10–15% and center it vertically so every part of the subject (including the man on the roof and the front wall base) sits entirely within the central 60% band of the canvas height (between 20% and 80%). Do not change palette, style, or any other elements.

problems: Steam curls are rising directly from the blue (cold) pool, contradicting the warm/cold pool distinction in the prompt.
fix: Remove all steam curls that originate from or hover immediately above the blue pool’s water surface (including the light-blue curl near the walkway if it appears to come from the blue pool). Keep the steam above the brick/red warm pool. If needed for balance, reposition one of the removed curls to rise from the red pool area instead. Do not change any other elements, colours, composition, textures, or proportions.

problems: Cuneiform-style text carved on the law stele violates the no-text rule
Cuneiform-like markings on the front trim of the left petitioner’s robe read as text
fix: Remove all text-like glyphs. On the law stele, delete the cuneiform panel and replace it with a solid charcoal #22211F area or a few non-glyph abstract blocks/hatching, keeping the relief figures and stele shape unchanged. On the petitioner’s robe, replace the vertical band of cuneiform-like strokes with a simple geometric trim (triangles/chevrons) using only the allowed inks (olive #A3AA6A, indigo #8F88B8, ochre #D9A441, charcoal #22211F). Change nothing else.

problems: Main subject (aqueduct and its buttressed piers) extends into the bottom margin and is not entirely within the middle 60% of the image height as required
fix: Select the entire aqueduct structure (deck, water channel, piers, and its right-hand abutment) and move it upward by about 10% of the image height so that no part of the aqueduct falls within the bottom 20% band. Preserve its perspective and connection to the city by raising the right-hand embankment/abutment to meet the shifted aqueduct. Fill any newly revealed area below with matching sand and scrub textures. Do not change colors, scale, or other elements.

problems: Subject extends into the bottom 20% of the canvas; not entirely within the middle 60% of the height
fix: On the existing 3:2 canvas with the #F3EBDB ground, select the entire subject group (palace facade, steps, columns, doorway, figures) and translate it upward by about 10–12% of canvas height so the lowest step/figure hem sits above the 20% bottom margin. If this pushes the top elements above the 80% upper limit, uniformly scale the subject down slightly (about 5–8%) to keep the entire subject contained between 20% and 80% of the canvas height. Do not alter colors, textures, composition balance, or add/remove any elements.

problems: Background vessels show triangular/lateen-style sails, anachronistic for 1000–600 BCE Phoenician ships which used square sails on yards
fix: Redraw the sails on all background boats as square or slightly rectangular sails hung from horizontal yards on single masts, appropriate to Phoenician vessels ca. 1000–600 BCE. Keep their sizes, positions, and the flat mid-century style; use only the existing four inks (blue for the sails), and change nothing else in the image.

problems: The terraces/hillside subject extends into the bottom and near the top margins, not entirely within the middle 60% of the image height as required.
fix: Scale down and vertically reposition the entire hillside-with-terraces group (including associated trees and rocks) so that every part of the terraces sits between 20% and 80% of the canvas height. Keep the 3:2 layout, colors limited to charcoal, olive, sage, and ochre on cream, and change nothing else.

problems: The cistern cutaway (main subject) extends beyond the middle 60% of the image height; top and bottom are too close to the edges.
fix: Group the entire subject (cistern cutaway, wellhead, rope and bucket, surrounding cut rock and small plants) and uniformly scale it down slightly, then recenter it so that the highest point of the subject sits below the 20% height line and the lowest point sits above the 80% height line. Keep the 3:2 canvas, colors, textures, and style unchanged; do not alter any other elements.

problems: The heap of murex shells looks mostly whole, not crushed as the prompt specifies
fix: Redraw the shell pile (including the lone shell in the foreground) as crushed murex fragments: irregular jagged pieces and broken spirals with exposed interiors, not intact shells. Keep the same placement, overall heap silhouette, and scale. Use only the existing four inks—charcoal #22211F for lines, olive #A3AA6A for shadows, plum #B07D9C and blue #8AA7C4 for shell surfaces and overprints. Maintain the flat cut-paper style and textures; change nothing else in the image.

problems: Foreground bevel-rim bowls (part of the subject) drop below the middle 60% of the image height
fix: Select the entire foreground subject group—the kiln, its mouth glow, nearby jars and bevel‑rim bowls, both figures, mudbrick stacks, their shadows, and the immediate ground patch they sit on—and translate it upward by about 10% of the canvas height so every subject element lies within the central 60% vertical band (between 20% and 80% of the height). Keep scale, colors (the four inks), textures, and horizontal placement unchanged. Leave the background river, reeds, distant buildings, boats, and sky as they are; allow the newly revealed lower area to remain the warm cream paper.

problems: The die block has an unexplained spout sticking out of its side, like a teapot.
The coins mix lion-stamped lumps with square-holed Chinese-style cash, which is out of place in Lydia.
fix: Remove the spout so the die is a plain block. Replace the two square-holed coins with irregular electrum lumps carrying the lion-head stamp, like the other two. Change nothing else.

problems: The porter walks up the colonnade's roof beam as if it were a ramp; the beam recedes in perspective and is not a walkway.
fix: Move the porter off the beam: stand him on the upper gallery behind its railing, or at ground level beside the far jars. Change nothing else.

problems: Missing the specified long ropewalk; only a large spool is shown.
Anachronistic modern-style lighthouse on the mole.
fix: Add a long ropewalk on the sandy yard parallel to the shoreline, within the middle 60% of the image height: a straight lane with evenly spaced low posts/hooks and 2–3 workers walking backward twisting strands. Render it in the existing palette (olive, bronze, charcoal; minimal blue), flat cut-paper style, and at the same scale as nearby figures. Replace the white cylindrical lighthouse with a Classical-era beacon: a small squat stone watch/beacon tower or pedestal with a brazier/fire basket on top, no glass lantern or railing. Keep colors to the four inks, preserve composition, and change nothing else.

problems: Triangular sailboat in the river is anachronistic for Ubaid-period Mesopotamia
Background architecture reads as a stepped ziggurat, more characteristic of later periods than Ubaid temples/platforms
fix: In the river, replace the triangular sailboat with a Ubaid-appropriate reed-bundle boat: low hull of bundled reeds and, if using a sail, a small square sail on a simple mast; alternatively depict poling or paddling without a sail. Keep scale and placement similar and use only the existing inks (charcoal #22211F, blue #8AA7C4, ochre #D9A441, sage #9DB592) with the same flat, cut-paper style. In the distant settlement, redesign the stepped ziggurat-like building into a lower Ubaid-period mudbrick temple/platform: a single-story or modest raised platform with buttressed walls and a flat roof, no multi-tiered stepped silhouette. Preserve its position, size, and palette, and change nothing else in the image.

problems: Main subject extends into the bottom 20% of the frame; not entirely within the middle 60% of the height.
Kilt shows decorative stripes/trim, conflicting with the prompt’s plain woven wool kilt.
fix: Move the runner and the immediate rocky ledge he stands on upward by about 10–15% of the canvas height so the entire figure (head to toes) sits between 20% and 80% of the frame height; keep the 3:2 composition and all other elements unchanged. Simplify the kilt by removing the decorative border stripes and colored tie, rendering it as a plain woven wool wrap in the approved ink palette (ochre with allowed overprint/charcoal accents), with no contrasting trim; change nothing else.

problems: Background temple shows later New Kingdom-style pylons/columns, anachronistic for Old Kingdom (c. 2600–2200 BCE).
fix: Replace the distant temple architecture with Old Kingdom-appropriate elements: low stone or mudbrick temple facades without pylons, mastabas, and/or a distant step pyramid silhouette. Keep scale, placement, palette (charcoal #22211F, blue #8AA7C4, teal #5E9C97, ochre #D9A441) and overall composition unchanged; do not alter the boats, net, figures, fish, reeds, birds, or water.

problems: Background sailboat has a triangular lateen-style sail, anachronistic for Old Kingdom Egypt
fix: Replace the triangular sail on the background boat with an Old Kingdom square/rectangular sail hung from a single vertical mast with a horizontal yard; keep the rigging minimal and stylised. Render the sail and mast using only the existing inks (blue #8AA7C4 and charcoal #22211F), preserving the flat mid-century style, composition, and all other elements unchanged.

problems: Cuneiform-like text visible on the clay tablet despite the no-text rule
fix: Remove all legible markings from the tablet/envelope. Replace them with a simple non-linguistic cylinder-seal impression: a narrow horizontal band of repeating geometric motifs rolled across the envelope, using only the existing inks (charcoal/blue/ochre/sage). Keep the tablet’s shape, shading/texture, and the rest of the image unchanged.

problems: Requested silver armlets are missing; the last bearer holds only bowls/vessels.
fix: Replace the two silver bowls in the fourth tribute-bearer’s hands with a pair of large Achaemenid-style silver armlets (open-ended bracelets with simple stamped motifs). Render them as flat shapes using charcoal halftone for the silver within the four-ink palette. Keep the bearer’s pose, scale, and all other elements unchanged, and ensure the composition remains within the middle 60% of the height.

problems: Seated elders are on separate brick blocks instead of a single low brick bench as specified
Group reads as two opposing rows rather than a clear semicircle around the speaker
fix: Replace the individual brick blocks under the seated elders with one continuous low brick bench in ochre-and-blue brick, integrated with the inner gate walls. Curve the bench subtly so the seated figures clearly form a shallow semicircle around the standing speaker. Nudge the seated elders’ positions minimally to align along this curved bench while keeping their poses, scale, and style unchanged. Update contact points and cast shadows to match the new continuous bench. Do not alter the palette, textures, gate, doors, background, or overall composition.

problems: Two teams appear to pull the sledge in opposite directions, which is physically unrealistic.
Background architecture looks like later New Kingdom temple pylons, anachronistic for the Old Kingdom setting.
Parts of the subject (foreground basket/canal edge) drop into the bottom 20% of the frame, violating the “middle 60% of the height” rule.
fix:
- Reconfigure the rope and workers so all pullers are clearly on the leading side of the sledge and oriented in the same direction; remove or reposition the rear line so no one appears to be pulling opposite the motion. Keep the sledge, block and rope palette unchanged.
- Replace the tall pylon-like temple structures with Old Kingdom-appropriate elements (e.g., a low pyramid under construction with a ramp, mastabas, causeway or quarry ramps). Maintain the same blue ink silhouettes and scaffolding style.
- Nudge the foreground canal edge and the bottom-right wicker basket upward so every element of the subject sits within the middle 60% of the image height. Do not introduce new elements or colors; keep the existing four-ink palette and overall composition otherwise unchanged.

problems: Visible Latin letter-like marks on the scribe’s clay tablet violate the no-text rule and are anachronistic.
Stack of bound books beside the scribe is anachronistic for the Neo‑Babylonian setting; should be clay tablets.
fix:
- On the seated scribe’s tablet, remove all letter-like glyphs. Repaint the tablet surface in ochre (#D9A441) with the existing texture; if desired, add a few tiny non-letter wedge impressions as abstract texture, not aligned like writing. Preserve the stylus and hand positions.
- Replace the stack of bound books at the scribe’s side with a small stack of rectangular clay tablets: flatten spines into solid slabs with slightly beveled edges, recolor to ochre (#D9A441) with charcoal (#22211F) edge accents and shadows. Do not add any readable marks. Keep their size, placement, and lighting consistent with the scene.
- Change nothing else.

problems: Twin steering oars are both on the same (starboard) side; period‑accurate twin quarter‑rudders should be one on each side of the stern.
fix: Reposition one of the two steering oars to the port side of the stern so the pair straddles the hull, keeping blade size, angle, and style identical. Remove the duplicate starboard oar so only one remains starboard. Add a small matching wake where the new port oar meets the water. Keep the helmsman’s hand on the starboard tiller only. Do not change the palette (#22211F, #8AA7C4, #5E9C97, #D9A441 on #F3EBDB), composition, textures, or any other elements.

problems: Visible cuneiform-like writing on the clay tablets violates the 'no text, letters, numbers' rule.
fix: On every clay tablet (the one being read, the stacked tablets, and those in the basket), remove the cuneiform glyphs. Replace them with blank faces or a subtle non-lettered stipple/halftone texture using only the approved inks (charcoal, blue, indigo, ochre). Do not add any characters, numerals, or legible symbols. Leave all other elements, colors, composition, and textures unchanged.

problems: Ringed Saturn, banded Jupiter and planets showing crescent phases need a telescope; a Babylonian watching with the naked eye saw only points of light.
fix: Replace every planet disc (the ringed one, the banded one, the half-lit ones and the plain discs) with a small bright star-like point of the same colour, slightly larger than the background stars, keeping each on its arc. Change nothing else.

problems: Jar exterior has strong horizontal bands, making it look decorated rather than plain as requested.
Cutaway ring shows diagonal grooves instead of clearly stacked coil cross-sections.
fix: Remove the dark horizontal banding on the jar; keep the body a plain teal field with only a subtle halftone texture (no stripes or decoration). In the cutaway ring, redraw the interior to depict discrete stacked coils in cross-section: render a series of closely stacked, slightly curved ochre bands across the wall thickness (ends of coils), not long diagonal grooves. Preserve the current composition, colours (charcoal, teal, brick, ochre on cream), shapes, shadows, and placement; change nothing else.

problems: River (part of the subject) touches the bottom edge, so the subject is not entirely within the middle 60% of the height
A small brown/orange vegetation patch introduces a fifth ink outside the specified palette
fix: 1) At the bottom-left corner, extend the cream paper #F3EBDB mask upward to trim the blue river so its lowest visible point sits within the central 60% band (at least 20% up from the bottom edge). Preserve the current river silhouette and flow; do not move other elements. 2) Recolour the lone warm brown/orange vegetation clump near the central fields to an approved ink—use sage #9DB592 (with optional charcoal #22211F texture). Ensure no residual orange hue remains and no additional colours are introduced.

problems: Teal is not the dominant colour; ochre and bronze occupy most of the area.
The small propeller-like crosspiece on the beam is anachronistic and unrealistic for a Sumerian ard.
One lower furrow band appears to extend in front of the plough tip instead of starting behind it.
fix: 1) Remove the little four-bladed, propeller-like cross at the left end of the beam; patch the beam silhouette with bronze #A97F63. If you need a yoke cue, replace it with a short single transverse peg or simple lashing, not a rotating cross. 2) Mask the furrow stripes so none of them extend in front of the black share; all stripes should begin exactly at (or a hair behind) the trailing edge of the share and radiate to the right. 3) Make teal #5E9C97 the dominant ink by recolouring every other furrow stripe to teal (keep the remainder in ochre #D9A441 and bronze #A97F63), and slightly extend the existing teal ground plane to the right under the furrows so the total teal area exceeds the others. Do not introduce any new colours or effects; change nothing else.

problems: The woven band floats in the middle of the warp, touching neither beam, while the weaver works at the empty near end; cloth is woven from one beam outward.
fix: Move the woven band so it starts at the beam nearest the weaver and grows away from her, with the beater resting at the band's far edge (the fell) and bare warp beyond it towards the far beam. Change nothing else.

problems: Image is rendered with photorealistic, 3D modeling and smooth gradients, violating the flat mid‑century style and the “no photorealism/3D/gradient” rule.
Palette appears to use continuous tones beyond the four specified inks, rather than flat spot colours/overprints.
fix: Rework the illustration into a flat cut‑paper, mid‑century print look: remove all volumetric shading and photoreal highlights from the tokens and bulla; fill each shape with flat colour and, if desired, a very subtle halftone or dry‑brush texture. Keep only simple, single‑tone shadows as flat teal shapes. Constrain the palette strictly to the four spot inks: background #F3EBDB; charcoal #22211F; dominant teal #5E9C97; ochre #D9A441; bronze #A97F63. Recolour any extra hues/gradients to the nearest of these inks and use overprint only where shapes overlap. Do not change the composition, arrangement, scale, or placement of the objects.

problems: Barley ears extend into the lower 20% of the canvas, so the subject is not entirely inside the middle 60% of the height.
fix: Select the barley ears (including their stems) and move the entire cluster upward by about 10–15% of the canvas height so the lowest tips sit above the bottom 20% band. Maintain their scale, colors (#D9A441 and #A97F63), textures, and overlap with the jar. Do not change any other elements.

problems: Oil lamp is a later closed-body form with a central fill hole rather than an open saucer lamp typical of the Chalcolithic Levant.
Lamp therefore does not match the prompt’s requirement for a “small open clay oil lamp.”
fix: Replace the current teardrop, closed oil lamp with an open Chalcolithic saucer lamp: a shallow round dish with a single pinched rim forming a wick channel. Use the existing bronze ink for the body, charcoal for the interior/shadow and wick tip, and ochre for the small flame. Keep the lamp’s scale, placement, lighting, and shadows consistent; change nothing else. Maintain the four-ink palette, flat mid-century style, and keep all elements within the middle 60% of the image height.

problems: The plumb line hangs from a point in mid-air at the top edge of the block, with nothing holding it.
fix: Hang the plumb line from something: a short wooden arm resting on the block's top edge, or the mason's raised hand. Change nothing else.

problems: Barley ear and its awns extend into the top 20% of the image, violating the "subject entirely inside the middle 60% of the height" rule.
Stylus reads as a modern wooden pencil (cylindrical body with decorative bands) rather than a simple pointed reed stylus appropriate to Uruk-period Mesopotamia.
fix:
- Reposition the barley ear downward (or shorten the stalk and awns) so that the highest awn tip sits within the central 60% of the canvas height; keep its scale and placement relative to the tablet and lines otherwise unchanged.
- Redraw the stylus as a natural reed: a slightly tapered hollow stem with a cut, chisel-like pointed tip; remove the decorative bands and any pencil-like detailing. Use only the specified inks (bronze #A97F63/ochre #D9A441 with charcoal #22211F line) and maintain its current size, angle, and shadow.

problems: Balance beam arms are unequal lengths, contradicting the specified equal-arm balance
fix: Extend the left side of the crossbeam so the distance from the central pivot to the left suspension ring matches the right side. Shift the left hanger and pan outward to that new ring position, keeping the current tilt angle, objects on the pans, colours, textures, grid, and all other elements unchanged.

problems: The olive branch and the grapevine are one continuous stem: olive leaves on the left turn into vine leaves and grapes on the right.
fix: Make them two separate plants: end the olive branch near the jar, and give the grapevine its own stem entering from the right behind the jar. They may cross, but neither may grow out of the other. Change nothing else.

problems: Tablet lacks a clear cylinder-seal impression even though the prompt specifies it is sealed
fix: Add a shallow rolled cylinder‑seal impression on the ochre clay tablet, ideally as a horizontal band near the right edge where the plum cylinder touches it. Depict the impression as recessed motif matching the seal’s figures, using only the existing inks (darker ochre with charcoal linework/halftone), in the same flat cut‑paper style. Change nothing else about composition, colours, textures, or placement.

problems: Headdress appears as a modern knit beanie with a pom-pom and horizontal stripes, not a Sumerian wool skullcap.
Staff is rendered solid charcoal/black, reading as metal or painted rather than a plain wooden staff as specified.
fix: Replace the headwear with a plain rounded Sumerian wool skullcap: remove the pom-pom and modern horizontal striping; use a smooth or lightly ribbed cap silhouette in indigo or teal with optional charcoal outline. Recolor the staff to read clearly as unpainted wood: switch the shaft from charcoal to ochre with a simple flat fill, keeping a thin charcoal edge only for outline. Change nothing else in composition, palette, scale, or textures.

problems: The overhead tree has narrow olive-like leaves; it should be a plane tree with broad lobed leaves as specified
fix: Replace only the foliage of the overhead tree: redraw the leaves as broad, palmate lobes (3–5 lobes each) characteristic of a plane tree (Platanus), keeping the same placements and density. Use only the existing ink palette (olive #A3AA6A with charcoal #22211F accents and permitted overprints). Preserve the trunk/branches, figures, diagram, composition, textures, and all other elements unchanged.

problems: Some iron ore nodules at the bottom extend outside the middle 60% of the image height, violating the placement rule for the subject
fix: Select the left and right foreground iron ore clusters and their scattered pebbles. Move them upward just enough so that their lowest points sit within the central 60% vertical band of the canvas (between 20% and 80% of image height). Preserve their sizes, colors, textures, and relative spacing. Do not change any other elements.

problems: Stylus appears as a modern pencil/pen with bands, not an Old Babylonian reed stylus (anachronism).
Tablet and stylus use photorealistic textures and gradients; not flat cut-paper planes and violates the no-3D/no-gradient rule.
Teal is not the dominant inked colour; the ochre/brown tablet visually dominates.
fix:
- Replace the tool with a historically accurate reed stylus: a short reed shaft cut to a wedge-shaped tip, no painted bands. Render it as a flat ochre #D9A441 shape with a single charcoal #22211F outline and a light halftone; remove any gradients or glossy highlights. Keep the current position and angle; shorten overall length to about two-thirds of the current to fit reed-stylus proportions.
- Repaint the clay tablet as a single flat cut-paper silhouette in ochre #D9A441 with only a subtle halftone/dry-brush texture; remove photographic pitting, rim shading and modeled lighting. Keep the incised square and diagonal as thin charcoal #22211F lines with crisp edges.
- Eliminate any remaining gradients on all elements.
- Make teal #5E9C97 the dominant colour by scaling up the teal background plane by ~25–30% (keep it behind the tablet, not touching the canvas edges) so it becomes the largest coloured shape after the paper background. Preserve the current composition and keep the subject within the middle 60% of the image height. Keep indigo #8F88B8 and other colours unchanged.

problems: Some of the smaller electrum fractions extend above/below the middle 60% of the canvas height, so the subject is not entirely within the required vertical band.
fix: On the 3:2 canvas (768 px tall), ensure all coin silhouettes fall between y=154 px (20%) and y=614 px (80%). Nondestructively translate only the small outer coins and their paired teal shadow shapes: move the top‑right coin group down ~90 px; move the lower‑left and lower‑right coin groups up ~90–110 px. Keep their radial arrangement around the large central coin. Do not change colors, textures, scale of the large coin, or any other elements.

problems: Map depicts most of Eurasia instead of only Achaemenid satrapies
Courier network extends far beyond the historical Royal Road within the empire
Cuneiform writing on tablets violates the 'no text' rule
fix:
- Edit the teal landmass so it only covers the Achaemenid Empire ca. 520–330 BCE (Anatolia to the Indus, Mesopotamia, Iran/Parthia, Levant, Egypt, and adjacent Central Asian satrapies). Convert any teal areas outside this footprint (Europe, far East Asia, etc.) back to the warm cream background.
- Constrain the ochre route network and rider silhouettes to the Royal Road system within the empire (e.g., Sardis–Susa with branches to Babylon, Ecbatana, Persepolis). Delete nodes, lines, and riders outside the corrected map area.
- Remove all cuneiform characters from the clay tablets. Keep the circular seal impressions, and if needed replace the writing with non-letter abstract texture marks that are not recognizable as script.
- Preserve the existing palette (charcoal, teal, indigo, ochre on warm cream), style, composition, and all other elements unchanged.

problems: The lintel over the gateway is segmented with vertical joints instead of being a single massive ashlar block as specified; joints over the span look structurally implausible.
fix: Replace the multi-block lintel spanning the opening with one continuous ashlar block. Remove all vertical joint lines across the lintel’s face and soffit; keep only a single horizontal joint line above and below where appropriate. Match the existing teal #5E9C97 fill, charcoal #22211F linework, and subtle texture so it blends seamlessly. Leave all other elements, colours, composition, and textures unchanged.

problems: Cuneiform-like writing on the clay tablets violates the “No text, letters, numbers” rule
fix: Remove all recognizable cuneiform or character-like markings from the clay tablets. Repaint the tablet faces using the existing three-ink palette as flat shapes with subtle halftone or dry-brush texture or random non-glyph scratches that do not form rows or symbols. Change nothing else in the image.

problems: Reed‑and‑palm garlands are missing; figures hold single fronds/branches instead of garlands.
Background boat has a triangular sail, anachronistic for Sumerian river craft; should be a square sail (or reed-bundle boat).
fix: Replace the palm fronds the villagers are holding with clear reed‑and‑palm garlands: braided or looped strands and/or wreaths made from reeds and palm leaves, held or draped, using only the existing inks (sage/ochre/brick/charcoal) and keeping the same flat, cut‑paper style. Redraw the river boat with a simple square or rectangular sail on a straight mast; optionally suggest a reed‑bundle hull. Do not add new colors, details, or elements; keep all other composition and spacing unchanged.

problems: Cracked canal bed and banks touch the bottom edge, so the subject is not entirely within the middle 60% of the height.
The sun sits high near the top edge, outside the middle 60% height band.
fix: On the existing 3:2 canvas, select the whole dried canal/riverbed and its banks as a group and move them upward so the lowest point of the cracked-earth shape sits above the lower 20% of the canvas height, leaving cream paper visible below. Then move the sun downward so the entire disc lies within the central 60% of the canvas height (between 20% and 80%). Keep all sizes, colors (#22211F, #C9705C, #D9A441) and textures unchanged; do not alter any other elements.

problems: Boat shows a triangular lateen sail, anachronistic for Pharaonic Egypt (should be a square sail).
The subject spills outside the middle 60% of the height; the farmer and forefield/dike dip into the lower margin.
fix: Redraw the river boat with period-appropriate rigging: a single vertical mast carrying a horizontal yard with a rectangular square sail set across the hull; remove the lateen boom and update the sail’s reflection to match the new square sail. Shift the entire foreground group (farmer, earthen dike, and silted field) upward by about 10–15% of the canvas height so every part of the subject sits between 20% and 80% of the image height. Keep the 3:2 layout, four-ink palette (charcoal, brick, blue, sage) on cream paper, and all other elements unchanged.

problems: No clearly depicted oxhide copper ingots on the quay, which the brief requires.
Some ships lack visibly twin steering oars (quarter-rudders); a few show only one.
Parts of the quay, jars, and figures extend into the bottom margin, so the subject is not entirely within the middle 60% of the height.
fix:
- Add two oxhide copper ingots on the quayside among the jars: flat, stylized ‘oxhide’ shapes with four corner lobes, rendered in the existing ink palette (brick/ochre with charcoal accents), no new colors.
- For each visible merchant ship, add the missing port-side steering oar so that every ship shows a matched pair of quarter-rudders mounted at the stern just below the gunwale, angled slightly into the water; keep scale and style consistent with the existing charcoal/brick shapes.
- Uniformly scale the illustrated scene down about 10% and nudge it upward so that all ships, quay, jars, and figures fall entirely within the central 60% of the image height; keep the 3:2 canvas, palette, and negative-space style unchanged.

problems: Parts of the rooftops and figures dip into the lower margin; the subject is not entirely within the middle 60% of the image height as required.
fix: Keep the 3:2 canvas. Select all illustrated content (rooftops, figures, city, Acropolis, smoke) and nudge it upward by about 6–8% of the canvas height so the lowest elements clear the bottom 20% band. Leave a clean band of warm cream #F3EBDB at the bottom. Verify the top of the smoke column still sits below the upper 20% band; if not, reduce the grouped content uniformly by up to 5% and re-center vertically. Do not alter colours, textures, or any other elements.

problems: Subject exceeds the middle 60% height band; flames and embers reach near the top and the base sits too close to the bottom
fix: Group the shelves, flames, and all embers/sparks as one subject. Uniformly scale the group down and reposition it so the highest flame/spark and the lowest base edge all sit within the vertical band between 20% and 80% of the canvas height (center it vertically). Remove or shift any stray sparks that still fall outside this band. Keep the 3-ink palette, textures, and all other elements unchanged.

problems: The balance hangs perfectly level with a coin in one pan and the other pan empty; it would tip towards the coin.
fix: Either place a small weight or a second coin in the empty right-hand pan so the level beam makes sense, or tilt the beam so the pan holding the coin hangs lower. Change nothing else.

problems: Knucklebones are depicted as modern spiky jacks, anachronistic for Classical Greece
fix: Replace the star‑shaped jacks near the crouching child with small, irregular bone‑like astragaloi (knucklebones). Draw 4–6 pebble/bone shapes, fingernail-sized, using only the existing inks (flat ochre or brick with charcoal outlines/shadows). Keep the children’s poses and all other elements unchanged; no new colours, text, or compositional shifts.

problems: Parts of the subject extend outside the middle 60% of the height (tree canopies into the top band; seated youths and blocks into the bottom band).
Anachronistic bound books on the ground at lower right; should be wax tablets or scrolls for Classical Athens.
fix:
- Reposition or slightly scale down the entire figure-and-tree group so every element (figures, plane trees, blocks) sits wholly within the central 60% of the image height, leaving clear negative space in the top and bottom 20% bands. Keep the 3:2 canvas and current palette/texture.
- Replace the two codex-like books at the lower right with a single closed wax tablet diptych (hinged wooden covers) or a small stack of wax tablets. Render in the existing four inks with flat shapes and the same style; no lettering added.

problems: Only two nobles and two guards are shown; the prompt requires three nobles each with a spearman guard (total six figures).
The guards’ sidearms are curved sabers; they should be Achaemenid akinakes (short, straight/leaf-shaped) at the belt.
Sword hilts are rendered in a yellow/gold hue outside the four specified inks.
fix: Add a third Persian noble in a kandys cloak and soft felt cap facing the throne from a different side (e.g., front-left of the dais) and place his spearman guard beside him holding a long spear; include an akinakes at the guard’s belt. Redraw all guards’ sidearms as Achaemenid akinakes: short, straight or slightly leaf-shaped blades with straight scabbards (no curvature), appropriate to 5th–4th c. BCE. Recolor all sword hilts/fittings currently shown as yellow/gold to one or a combination (overprint) of the allowed inks only: brick #C9705C, indigo #8F88B8, plum #B07D9C, or charcoal #22211F. Keep the existing throne, dais, figures, style, inks, and composition unchanged aside from adding the missing noble-and-guard pair and correcting the swords; ensure all elements remain within the central 60% of the image height.

problems: Subject elements extend outside the middle 60% of the height (feet at the bottom edge; spear tips and wall crenellations near the top edge)
Hieroglyphic/letter-like markings on the gate violate the no-text rule
fix:
- Uniformly scale down the entire illustrated subject group (mercenaries, spears, gate and walls) by about 15–20% and reposition it so all parts lie entirely within the central 60% band of the canvas height, leaving at least the top and bottom 20% as untouched cream negative space. Keep the 3:2 canvas, colors, and left-right composition unchanged.
- Remove all hieroglyphic/letter-like inscriptions from the gate surfaces and lintel. Replace them with plain painted panels or simple non-textual pictograms (e.g., sun disk and figures without glyph columns), using only the existing inks (charcoal #22211F, brick #C9705C, bronze #A97F63, indigo #8F88B8) and the same flat/overprint texture. Change nothing else.

problems: The crescent moon's lit side faces away from the sun; a crescent's bright edge always faces the sun.
fix: Mirror the crescent moon so its bright, convex edge faces down and to the right, towards the sun on the horizon. Change nothing else.

problems: The bards’ instruments aren’t chelys-lyres; they look like box-bodied kitharas rather than rounded tortoise-shell lyres specified by the prompt.
fix: Redraw both instruments as chelys-lyres: replace the rectangular/box bodies with rounded tortoise-shell resonators (oval, slightly domed). Have two gently curved arms rise from the shell to a straight crossbar, with 7 taut strings anchored at the shell. Use only the existing inks (charcoal for frame/strings, brick/ochre/plum for fills and overprints) and keep all poses, composition, and other elements unchanged.

problems: Astronomer-priests are not pointing in two directions; they all indicate to the right.
Parts of the subject exceed the middle 60% of the canvas height (comet tail near the top edge and lower ziggurat mass at the bottom).
The tripod-mounted curved sighting device reads as a later quadrant/sextant, anachronistic for the Neo-Babylonian period.
fix:
- Repose the leftmost astronomer so he turns slightly left and extends his right arm to point left; keep his left hand holding the star tablet. Leave the other two figures pointing right.
- Lower the entire comet streak so its highest point sits below the 80% height line; keep the nucleus and tail fully within the central 60% band. If needed, slightly shorten the topmost wisp of the tail to stay inside this band.
- Remove or crop the extra lower tiers of the ziggurat so the lowest visible part of the subject (parapet/figures’ feet) sits above the 20% height line; keep the 3:2 canvas size unchanged.
- Replace the tripod instrument with a simple gnomon or measuring rod appropriate to Neo-Babylonia, or remove the instrument entirely. Maintain the existing four-ink palette and flat mid-century style for any adjusted elements.

problems: Background settlement and tall cypress-like trees look like a later Mediterranean village, not Neolithic Levant (anachronism)
Children’s tailored tunics and the headband read as later/modern rather than simple Neolithic garments
Only one child (foreground) shows clearly purple-stained fingertips; the rear child’s hands—and the foreground child’s other hand—aren’t visibly stained
fix:
- Replace the distant architecture with early Neolithic Levant structures: small round or simple rectangular mudbrick huts with flat roofs clustered on a tell; remove tower-like forms and modern village silhouettes. Replace the tall cypress-like trees with low scrub or sparse short trees typical of the Levant. Keep forms flat and stylized in the existing 4-ink palette.
- Modify the children’s clothing to simple Neolithic wraps or short untailored shifts; remove visible seams and the headband on the foreground child. Keep shapes and silhouettes similar and use only the existing inks (brick/ochre/plum with charcoal line) and overprint texture.
- Add clear plum (#B07D9C) stains to the fingertips and palms of both children’s berry-holding and picking hands; add a subtle plum smudge to the foreground child’s other hand as well. Apply as overprinted flat shapes consistent with the current texture. Change nothing else.

problems: Background ships have triangular/lateen-style sails that are anachronistic for Phoenician c. 800–600 BCE, which should use square sails.
